title: Diagonal collapse of an indexed sum
statement:
Let $\alpha$ be a finite type with decidable equality, let $h \colon \alpha \times \alpha \to \bbr$ be any function, and let $c \in \bbr$. Summing $h(y,z)$ against the weight that equals $c$ when $y = z$ and $0$ otherwise, over all ordered pairs, leaves only the diagonal terms:
\[
  \sum_{(y,z)\,\in\,\alpha \times \alpha} h(y,z)\cdot\bigl(\text{$c$ if $y = z$, else $0$}\bigr)
    \;=\; \sum_{y\,\in\,\alpha} h(y,y)\cdot c.
\]
hypotheses_covered: h is a real-valued function on α × α
replaced:
For a finite type $\alpha$ with decidable equality, a function $h : \alpha \to \alpha
\to \mathbb{R}$, and a scalar $c \in \mathbb{R}$,
\[
  \sum_{(y_1, y_2) : \alpha \times \alpha} h(y_1, y_2)
    \cdot [\![y_1 = y_2]\!] \cdot c
  \;=\; \sum_{y : \alpha} h(y, y) \cdot c,
\]
where $[\![\cdot]\!]$ denotes the indicator of the condition.
